questions.q: Which structure is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
questions.x: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole. Both cell types have a membrane, a nucleus and mitochondria.

questions.q: Cells in the pancreas make and secrete large amounts of digestive enzymes. Which organelle would you expect these cells to have in large amounts?
questions.x: Enzymes are proteins. Ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum make them, and the Golgi body packages them for secretion.

questions.q: A red blood cell is placed in distilled water. What happens to it?
o: It shrinks as water leaves by osmosis.
It swells and bursts as water enters by osmosis.
It stays the same because its cell wall resists the pressure.
It swells as salts diffuse into it.
questions.x: Distilled water has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm, so water enters by osmosis. An animal cell has no cell wall, so it swells and bursts.

questions.q: Equal strips of potato were left in sucrose solutions. They gained mass in 0.1 and 0.2 mol dm⁻³, did not change in mass in 0.3 mol dm⁻³, and lost mass in 0.4 and 0.5 mol dm⁻³. What can be concluded?
o: The potato cells contain 0.3 mol dm⁻³ of sucrose.
The water potential of the potato cells is about equal to that of 0.3 mol dm⁻³ sucrose solution.
Sucrose diffused into the strips in the weaker solutions.
The potato cells were dead, so no osmosis took place at 0.3 mol dm⁻³.
questions.x: No net movement of water means the water potentials inside and outside are equal. The cell sap contains many solutes, not just sucrose, so its sucrose concentration cannot be stated.

questions.q: Which test result shows that a food contains reducing sugar?
o: A brick-red precipitate forms on heating with Benedict's solution.
A violet colour forms with biuret solution.
A white emulsion forms with ethanol and water.
questions.x: Reducing sugars give a green, yellow, orange or brick-red precipitate when heated with Benedict's solution. Blue-black iodine shows starch, and violet biuret shows protein.

questions.q: The activity of an enzyme falls sharply when the temperature rises above 40 °C. Why?
o: The enzyme is killed by the heat.
The active site changes shape, so the substrate no longer fits.
The molecules move more slowly, so there are fewer collisions.
The enzyme is used up in the reaction.
questions.x: High temperature breaks bonds that hold the enzyme's shape, so it is denatured. Enzymes are molecules, not living things, so they are not 'killed'.

questions.q: Where are most digested food molecules absorbed into the blood?
questions.x: The small intestine has villi and microvilli that give a large surface area, with capillaries close to the surface. The large intestine mainly absorbs water.

questions.q: Which statement about bile is correct?
o: It contains lipase, which digests fats.
It is made in the gall bladder.
It emulsifies fats, increasing their surface area for lipase.
It breaks fats down into fatty acids and glycerol.
questions.x: Bile contains no enzymes. It is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder, and it breaks fat into small droplets so lipase can work faster.

questions.q: What are the raw materials of photosynthesis?
questions.x: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, using light energy absorbed by chlorophyll.

questions.q: A plant is kept at 25 °C in bright light in normal air. Increasing the light intensity further does not increase its rate of photosynthesis. Which change is most likely to increase the rate?
o: Increase the light intensity even more.
questions.x: Light is no longer the limiting factor. In bright light at a warm temperature, the low CO₂ concentration of normal air (about 0.04 %) limits the rate.

questions.q: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.x: The pulmonary vein is the vein that carries oxygenated blood, from the lungs to the left atrium. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.

questions.q: Why is the muscular wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right ventricle?
o: The left ventricle holds a larger volume of blood.
The left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body, which needs a higher pressure.
The left ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood.
The left ventricle receives blood from the lungs at high pressure.
questions.x: The right ventricle only pumps blood to the nearby lungs. The left must create a higher pressure to push blood around the whole body. Both ventricles pump the same volume.

questions.q: What is produced by anaerobic respiration in human muscle?
questions.x: In human muscle, glucose → lactic acid, releasing a little energy. Ethanol and carbon dioxide are the products in yeast.

questions.q: After a sprint, an athlete keeps breathing quickly and deeply for several minutes. Why?
o: To remove the lactic acid through the lungs.
To take in oxygen to break down the lactic acid built up during anaerobic respiration.
To replace the glucose used during the sprint.
questions.x: The sprint built up an oxygen debt. Extra oxygen is needed to oxidise the lactic acid, which is carried to the liver; the lactic acid is not breathed out.

questions.q: Which hormone lowers blood glucose concentration, and which organ secretes it?
questions.x: The pancreas secretes insulin when blood glucose is high. Insulin makes the liver and muscles convert glucose to glycogen. Glucagon has the opposite effect.

questions.q: On a hot day a person sweats a lot and drinks little water. Which describes what happens?
o: Less ADH is secreted, and a large volume of dilute urine is produced.
More ADH is secreted, the collecting ducts become more permeable to water, and a small volume of concentrated urine is produced.
More ADH is secreted, the collecting ducts become less permeable to water, and a large volume of urine is produced.
Less ADH is secreted, and more water is reabsorbed into the blood.
questions.x: Water loss lowers the blood's water potential. The pituitary gland releases more ADH, which makes the collecting ducts more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed and the urine is small in volume and concentrated.

questions.q: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant to short (t). A heterozygous tall plant is crossed with a short plant. What is the expected ratio of tall to short offspring?
questions.x: Tt × tt gives Tt and tt in equal numbers, so tall : short = 1 : 1. A 3 : 1 ratio comes from crossing two heterozygotes.

questions.q: Albinism is caused by a recessive allele. Two parents without albinism have a child with albinism. They then have a second child who does not have albinism. What is the probability that this second child carries the albinism allele?
questions.x: Both parents must be heterozygous (Aa × Aa), giving AA : Aa : aa = 1 : 2 : 1. The child has no albinism, so aa is ruled out: of the 3 remaining equal chances, 2 are Aa. The probability is 2/3.

questions.q: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, which organism is the primary consumer?
questions.x: The primary consumer eats the producer. Grass is the producer, so the grasshopper is the primary consumer.

questions.q: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, the grass fixes 20 000 kJ of energy. About 10 % of the energy passes from one trophic level to the next. How much energy reaches the frogs?
questions.x: Grasshoppers get 10 % of 20 000 = 2000 kJ, and frogs get 10 % of 2000 = 200 kJ. The rest is lost mainly as heat from respiration, and in faeces and uneaten parts.
